title: The Power of Authenticity: How Leading Brands Are Pulling Ahead in Creator Marketing
gist: BCG's survey of 940 marketers finds creator marketing is a $30B+ industry growing 1.5x faster than overall marketing budgets, yet only 15% of marketers run an operating model that captures full value. Leaders win via trust-based creator selection, freedom briefs, integrated fee-plus-boosting budgets, full-funnel and LLM share-of-model measurement, a single accountable owner, and keeping judgment in-house while outsourcing execution to agencies.

insights.speaker: Derek Rodenhausen
insights.so_what: Budget share is shifting from brand-scripted ads toward creators; beneficiaries include creator platforms and influencer agencies.

insights.so_what: Most brands are under-optimized, leaving a large capability gap for leaders to exploit and for consultancies/agencies to sell into.

insights.claim: The creator ecosystem is maturing as creator sourcing platforms, specialist influencer marketing agencies, and full-funnel measurement tools start to operate at scale, making inaction increasingly costly.

insights.claim: Key gaps remain in creator marketing: measuring organic impressions and full-funnel impact is complex, creator negotiation and management is still largely manual, and most organizations lack staffing and ownership beyond one-off campaigns.

insights.so_what: Creator content becomes an input to generative-engine optimization; brands under-investing risk invisibility in AI shopping answers.

insights.claim: High-performing marketers are 12 percentage points more likely to prioritize audience trust over follower count or rates, and weight past creator performance more heavily (46% vs. 36%) while de-emphasizing reach and cost.
insights.speaker: Derek Rodenhausen
insights.so_what: Selection criteria are moving from reach/CPM toward trust and track record.
insights.quote: High performers are 12 percentage points more likely than other marketers to prioritize audience trust over follower count or rates.

insights.claim: Leaders brief creators for freedom—a minimal set of dos and don'ts plus one or two inspirational ideas—because over-scripting undercuts the credibility creators are hired for, whereas templatized briefs get skimmed and yield inconsistent output.
insights.speaker: Derek Rodenhausen
insights.so_what: Less control yields better output; brand teams should cut brief length and review burden.
insights.quote: a creator brings their own credibility to a brand, and over-scripting undercuts the reason they were hired
insights.locator: Leaders, on the other hand, brief for freedom.

insights.claim: One global consumer brand built community-specific briefs and ran three live briefing sessions with creators, agency, and brand together, cutting rework by 30% to 50%.
insights.speaker: Derek Rodenhausen
insights.so_what: Creator camps / live briefings are a measurable efficiency lever.
insights.quote: cutting rework by 30% to 50%
insights.locator: Leaders also run creator camps.

insights.claim: Leaders are 10 percentage points more likely to build long-term creator partnerships, structured with pre-negotiated terms for future content, standing usage rights and a standard rate card, enabling fast activation for launches or trends.
insights.speaker: Derek Rodenhausen
insights.so_what: Creators shift from spot buys to retained relationships, favoring creators with brand-safe longevity.

insights.claim: Leaders are 1.5 times more likely to have a single accountable owner per brand connecting brand, PR and media, and cross-functional collaboration is the widest capability gap between leaders and others (15 percentage points).

insights.so_what: Organizational design, not budget, is the binding constraint for most brands.

insights.claim: Leaders are 1.3 times more likely to run creator marketing as its own function with a dedicated team of four or more FTEs, supported by tools, in-house analytics and AI review tools trained on brand guidelines for first-pass creative review.

insights.claim: 75% of brands work with at least one influencer marketing agency, but leaders keep strategy and planning in-house 85% of the time and briefing/creative direction 69% of the time, versus 37% for day-to-day execution and 47% for paid boosting.

insights.so_what: Agencies are being pushed toward execution/logistics roles, compressing their strategic value capture.

insights.claim: BCG recommends starting with a self-assessment against eight practices, then building a discovery engine, naming an accountable owner with budget authority across creator fees, boosting and affiliates, consolidating fragmented spend buckets, refining measurement, and planning for scale and automation.
